hwinfoSensorMap.resolutionMethod: Temps.ini references #HWiNFO-TEMPS-<CHANNEL>-SensorId/SensorInstance/EntryId# which @Include from @Resources/HWiNFO.inc. Rainmeter variable names are case-insensitive, so #HWiNFO-TEMPS-MOBO-...# in Temps.ini resolves to the HWiNFO-TEMPS-MoBo-... keys in HWiNFO.inc.

TCPU_VCORE.inferredMeaning: CPU Vcore (Volts) -- inferred from the user's 'VCORE' relabel and the displayed magnitude (~1.2-1.5V range implied by the hand-edited warn thresholds 1.1/1.3/1.4/1.5). SensorId 0xf7006687 is the same physical Super-I/O/EC chip used elsewhere in HWiNFO.inc for 'CPU Fan' and chassis fans (entry ids 0x3000000-0x3000003); entry 0x2000012 is otherwise undocumented in this HWiNFO.inc, consistent with it being a repurposed/added voltage entry not present in the original fan/temp mappings.
TCPU_VCORE.confidence: inferred, not independently verified against a live HWiNFO shared-memory dump

TGPU1_GPUVOLT.inferredMeaning: GPU core voltage (Volts) -- same physical GPU sensor/instance (0xe0002000 / 0x14) as all other GPU1-* entries in HWiNFO.inc (Usage=0x7000000, original Temp=0x1000000, Fan%=0x8000000, FanRPM=0x3000000, MemAlloc=0x80000fc, MemUsg=0x7000008, Clock=0x6000000, MemClock=0x6000004); entry 0x2000000 does not collide with any of those, consistent with HWiNFO's typical GPU sensor ordering where a voltage entry follows the temperature entry. Warn thresholds hand-edited to 0.85/0.95/1.0/1.05 support a GPU-core-voltage magnitude.

TGPU2_CPUPOWER.inferredMeaning: CPU package power (Watts) -- SensorId 0xf0002a00 appears nowhere else in HWiNFO.inc (the original GPU2 channel used 0xf0000ff0); the 0xf000xxxx range is used elsewhere in this file for CPU/system-class sensors (CPU temp 0xf0000400, CPU clock 0xf0000300, drive temps 0xf0000100), so 0xf0002a00 is plausibly a distinct 'CPU power/enhanced sensor' group added by the user, with entry 0x5000000 as its package/total power reading. Warn thresholds hand-edited to 50/100/150/200W support a CPU-power magnitude (screenshot shows ~62W current / 125W max).

TMOBO_GPUPOWER.inferredMeaning: GPU board/total power draw (Watts) -- same physical GPU sensor/instance as TGPU1 (0xe0002000 / 0x14); entry 0x5000000 does not collide with any other documented GPU1 entry in this file, consistent with being the GPU's 'Power' reading. Warn thresholds hand-edited to 50/150/200/250W support a GPU-power magnitude (screenshot shows ~47W current / 80W max).

backgroundGeometry.coordinateSpace: All numbers below are UNSCALED design-space units. Every meter in the skin (including this one) carries TransformationMatrix = Scale;0;0;Scale;Scale;Scale = 1.7;0;0;1.7;1.7;1.7, i.e. the whole design is uniformly scaled 1.7x AND then translated +1.7,+1.7 device px. Apply that matrix once to every unscaled coordinate given anywhere in this document to get final device pixels.

verticalFlowSummary: Panel is a single rounded background box (title strip + body) auto-sized to its content. Layout order top-to-bottom: [Title 'POWER' centered, Y=9 abs] -> [Row1 VCORE: Label(left,X=7)/Value(right,X=197)/Max(center,X=103) all at Y=32 abs] -> [Row2 GPU VOLT: same 3-column layout, Y = Row1's rendered bottom + RowSpacing(1)] -> [Row3 CPU POWER: Y = Row2's bottom + 1] -> [Row4 GPU POWER: Y = Row3's bottom + 1] -> [6 more rows for CHIP/RAM/AIR/PSU/DRIVE1/DRIVE2, each identical 3-column layout PLUS a 1px horizontal Bar meter beneath, but ALL SIX ARE HIDDEN/DISABLED so contribute zero height/content] -> [invisible MeterBackgroundHeight spacer, 11px below the last visible content, whose Y stamps the total content height used to auto-size the rounded background]. Within every visible row, the Max (session-max) meter and Value (current-reading) meter both copy the Y of the meter immediately preceding them in the file via 'Y=r' (exact same Y, not stacked below) -- this is what keeps Label/Value/Max visually on one horizontal line despite being 3 separate meter objects. All coordinates are unscaled design units; a uniform TransformationMatrix (scale 1.7, translate +1.7/+1.7) is applied per-meter to reach final device pixels. NO progress bars are rendered anywhere on the POWER panel's 4 visible rows -- only the 6 hidden legacy temperature rows have Bar meters defined.
notes: CRITICAL: For the 4 active rows (VCORE/GPU VOLT/CPU POWER/GPU POWER), the measureTempXPerc Calc measures and their IfCondition/IfTrueAction/IfFalseAction BarColor logic reference meter names (meterTempCpuBar, meterTempGpu1Bar, meterTempGpu2Bar, meterTempMoBoBar) that DO NOT EXIST as meter sections in Temps.ini. This is leftover/dead code from the original temperature-bar skin: it runs every tick but has no visual output. A pixel-perfect reproduction should render ONLY the 3 text columns per row (label, value, max) and NO bar underneath.

CRITICAL: warn-color thresholds for the 4 active rows were hand-edited as literal numeric constants directly inside each measureTempXValueWarn Formula line (Volts for VCORE/GPU VOLT: 1.1/1.3/1.4/1.5 and 0.85/0.95/1.0/1.05; Watts for CPU POWER/GPU POWER: 50/100/150/200 and 50/150/200/250). The corresponding #TXWarnTh1..4# variables in Variables.inc still hold their original Celsius-oriented values (25/45/60/70 etc.) and are NOT used by these four channels' color logic -- only by the hidden/disabled Chipset/RAM/Air/PSU/Drive1/Drive2 rows, which still use the variable-driven form.

The '#TXMax#' variables (TCPUMax=70, TGPU1Max=95, TGPU2Max=95, TMOBOMax=95) are still referenced by measureTempXPerc for the 4 active channels, producing a near-meaningless percentage (e.g. a ~1.3V VCORE reading / 70 = ~1.9%) -- harmless since it only ever fed the now-nonexistent bar meters.

The Max/session-max value is computed purely in Rainmeter via a self-referential Calc formula 'Max(measureX, measureXMax)' -- i.e. it is NOT sourced from any separate HWiNFO 'max' entry id. A custom renderer must replicate this by keeping its own running max-since-launch (or since-reset) per channel, seeded by the first reading, and it resets whenever the skin/renderer process restarts (Rainmeter has no built-in persistence for these Calc measures across sessions).

Text FontColor for the '%1' current-value meters is DYNAMIC, wired to FontColor=[measureTempXValueWarn] with DynamicVariables=1 -- i.e., the big current-value number changes color live based on the voltage/wattage thresholds tables above (blue -> yellow -> orange -> red -> dark red), while the row LABEL stays fixed black (0,0,0,205) and the grayed 'Max: ...' text stays fixed gray (120,120,120,255) regardless of value.

Number formatting as literally authored in Temps.ini: VCORE and GPU VOLT use Text="%1 V" / "Max: %1 V" with NumOfDecimals=3 (e.g. '1.268 V', 'Max: 1.308 V'). CPU POWER and GPU POWER use Text="%1W" / "Max: %1W" with NumOfDecimals=0 (Max explicit, Value defaulted) -- NOTE these have NO SPACE between the number and the unit letter (e.g. '62W', 'Max: 125W'), which differs from the reference screenshot's rendering, which appeared to show '62 W' / '125 W' with a space and did not show a 'V' suffix for the voltage rows at all. Since the .ini text is the ground truth for the skin's logic, this spec transcribes the .ini literally and flags the discrepancy -- worth a quick visual double-check against the actual running skin if byte-exact spacing matters.

The outer background 'frame' stroke (Shape7 in StyleBackground) is defined with StrokeColor 96,138,203/alpha100 but Stroke_Width=0 in Variables.inc, so the computed StrokeWidth is 0 and the frame is not actually visible in this skin instance -- do not render a visible outline unless Stroke_Width is later changed.

HWiNFO sensor id/entry id numeric values for the 4 active channels are transcribed exactly as found in HWiNFO.inc (case-insensitive variable match: Temps.ini's #HWiNFO-TEMPS-MOBO-...# resolves to HWiNFO.inc's mixed-case HWiNFO-TEMPS-MoBo-... keys). Their *meaning* (Vcore/GPU-volt/CPU-power/GPU-power) is inferred from the user's label overrides, the hand-edited threshold magnitudes, and non-collision with other documented entry ids on the same physical sensor/instance -- it was NOT verified against a live HWiNFO shared-memory/sensor-panel dump, which is the only way to get an authoritative unit+description for a raw SensorId/EntryId pair. Treat the 'inferredMeaning' fields as best-effort labeling, not certainty.

Global Update=1000 (root [Rainmeter] section) drives the base 1Hz refresh. All 4 active Plugin (HWiNFO) measures use the default UpdateDivider (effectively 1, i.e. every tick). Their dependent Calc measures (Max/Perc/ValueWarn) use UpdateDivider=-1 and instead recompute via explicit OnChangeAction chains ([!UpdateMeasureGroup ...]) fired whenever the parent Plugin measure's value changes -- a Rainmeter performance pattern, not a different effective refresh rate; treat all four rows as updating at ~1 Hz.

Styles.inc and Variables.inc were not in the original required-reads list but were additionally opened to resolve @IncludeStyles/@IncludeVariables and cross-check the pre-resolved GLOBAL VARIABLES/GLOBAL STYLES given in the task; all figures above (StyleBackground geometry, TopMarginFormula/ContentMarginFormula/RightAlign/ContentWidth/CenterAlign derivations, per-style X/Y/font defaults) were confirmed to match.

MeasureSettingsScript (Measure=Script, Settings.lua) and the Group=Controls meters (ControlSettings_/ControlSettings, a hover-revealed gear icon opening a settings config) are Rainmeter-interaction plumbing unrelated to the temps/power data display; included/noted for completeness but not required for a static/data-driven D2D re-render.
